title: The Participant Journey: From Front Door to Follow-Up
description: A walk through the complete WIOA Title I journey for Adult, Dislocated Worker, and Youth customers: sign-in, registration, eligibility, participation, services, outcomes, exit, follow-up, and validation. Each step is taught with who does it, what document it produces, and which rule governs it, using California's state spine and the learner's own local policy.
notes: Audience: All AJCC frontline staff, partner staff. Format: HD or LV. Hours assumed from format (HD = 4 hours). Gap addressed: No published process map of the California participant journey exists; the closest is San Bernardino County's prose desk manual.
learning_objectives: Distinguish a reportable individual from a participant and identify the service that starts participation for each program.
Sequence the 12 major steps of the participant journey and name the artifact and governing directive for each.
Explain the 90-day exit rule and which activities do and do not extend the exit clock.
Identify which decisions in their center are governed by state rule and which are delegated to local policy.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Reportable Individuals vs. Participants; The 12-Step Participant Journey; Exit and the 90-Day Clock; State Rule vs. Local Policy. The closing project ("Project: Map One Customer's Journey") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a participant-journey walkthrough of a realistic customer file, naming the role, artifact, and governing rule at each step) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (HD or LV; HD = 4 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Design driver (catalog "gap addressed"): No published process map of the California participant journey exists; the closest is San Bernardino County's prose desk manual. Statistics and audit findings quoted from the catalog have not been independently verified.
